title: primary-source-verification coverage-record
description: psv's TOP-LINE output — the honest coverage disclosure. Carries the named signal `oracle_verified_under_known_coverage` (the ONLY permitted top-line string; `correctness_converged` is FORBIDDEN and never appears — enforced by coverage_policy_check.py) and the per-claim counts N/R/W/K of M. The coverage disclosure, NOT a boolean, is the contract (proposal §3 step 4, §9 Q3). Analogous to csr's split: psv emits doc-findings (per-claim defects) AND this coverage-record (the top-line disclosure). M=0 (no source-admissible claims — e.g. a purely interpretive doc) and K>0 (claims extracted but unverifiable) both ESCALATE to a human, never a silent pass (rule 3). Carries `rightness: human_confirm_required` as a constant — a coverage disclosure never certifies the doc is right.

artifact.description: Path/ref to the doc-shaped artifact whose claims were verified.

signal.description: The sole permitted top-line signal. psv NEVER emits 'correctness_converged' or any boolean 'the doc is correct' — coverage_policy_check.py asserts this string is the only top-line value present.

counts.description: N/R/W/K of M. coverage_policy_check.py asserts total_extracted = verified + refuted + narrowed + unverifiable.

verified.description: N — claims the fetched source supports (model found no contradiction; not a proof of none — comparison blind-spot caveat). Counted here, NOT listed as findings.

refuted.description: R — claims the fetched source contradicts (each a blocker finding with a fetched quote).

narrowed.description: W — claims the fetched source supports only in a weaker form (each a warning finding with a fetched quote).

unverifiable.description: K — claims no fetchable source could adjudicate (interpretive / paywalled / judgment call). Each escalates to a human.

total_extracted.description: M — total atomic source-admissible claims extracted. M = N + R + W + K. M=0 means psv had no admissible surface on this artifact → escalates to a human (distinct from K>0).

rightness.description: Outcome-axis constant. A coverage disclosure NEVER changes this — psv does not judge whether the doc is right.

claim_ref.description: The unverifiable claim's location/id, when this escalation is a K>0 claim. Absent for the M=0 (no surface) escalation.

reason.description: Why it escalates: 'no fetchable source adjudicates it' (K>0) or 'no source-admissible claims extracted — psv has no surface on this artifact' (M=0).

escalations.description: Human escalations: every K>0 claim (one entry each) PLUS one M=0 entry when total_extracted=0. Never empty when K>0 or M=0.

coverage.description: Honest coverage notes (workspace rule 3): the extractor blind-spot (claims neither party could see are absent from M) and the comparison blind-spot (`verified` ≠ 'no contradiction exists'), plus any source-fetch degradation. Never silent.

claim_ref.description: The claim id whose adjudication source is volatile.

volatile_source.description: Where the source lived at run time (e.g. ~/.claude/projects/... memory files, /tmp clones, shell environment state). Volatile = repo-external / unversioned / deletable.

volatile_authority_registry.description: Volatile-authority registry (fix B): one entry per claim adjudicated against a non-durably-re-fetchable source. Covers verified claims too — their sources are counted-not-listed in the packet, so this registry is their only re-fetchability signal. Absent/empty when no volatile sources were used.
